cf.title: add missed tests for gist index

input.subject: [PATCH] add missed tests for gist index

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal: the patches are test-only and raise gistxlog.c coverage from about 18% to about 84%. The three surviving objections are fixable. already-exists-1 asks what 0002 adds beyond 027_stream_regress.pl, maintenance-fit-2 asks for the added runtime, and prior-attempts-1 asks how page recycling is made deterministic in a parallel regression group. A committer who knows GiST vacuum would want these answered before commit.

brief.title: Add GiST tests for page recycling, deleting all entries, and redo
brief.problem: The gist regression test vacuums only once after deleting rows, so emptied leaf pages are never recycled or reused, and no test deletes every entry. No test replays a GiST page deletion through recovery, and the redo side of gistxlog.c went unexecuted.
brief.proposed_design: 0001 adds more vacuum, delete-all and reuse steps to gist.sql. 0002 adds a recovery TAP test that runs the same workload with wal_consistency_checking set, then crashes and restarts the server. Both tests compare an index scan against a sequential scan.
author_claims: Line coverage of src/backend/access/gist rises from 80.3% to 87.9%.
Coverage of gistxlog.c rises from about 18% to about 84%, and gistvacuum.c from about 59% to about 91%.
brief.thread_state: Sho Ito reported that v3 passes the gist regression test and the new TAP test on master; the author has since posted v4 as a rebase. No committer has replied, and nobody has commented on test runtime or design.
unclear: The material does not give the runtime the new recovery test and the extra gist.sql steps add.
The thread does not say how the test makes sure deleted pages are old enough to be recycled, which affects whether the test is stable across runs and platforms.
The thread does not say whether wal_consistency_checking is set for the whole TAP test or only for the GiST workload.
The CommitFest entry targets "stable", but the thread does not say whether the tests are meant for back branches.
The TAP test number changed from 057 to 061 between versions, so it may collide with other new tests.

prior_attempts.title: Revert "Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin"
prior_attempts.quote: This test proved to be unstable on the buildfarm, timing out before the standby could catch up on 32-bit machines where more rows were required and failing to reliably trigger multiple index vacuum rounds on 64-bit machines where fewer rows should be required.
prior_attempts.reason:
This reverts commit aa607980aee08416211f003ab41aa750f5559712.

This test proved to be unstable on the buildfarm, timing out before the
standby could catch up on 32-bit machines where more rows were required
and failing to reliably trigger multiple index vacuum rounds on 64-bit
machines where fewer rows should be required.

Because the instability is only known to be present on versions of
Postgres with TIDStore used for dead TID storage by vacuum, this is only
being reverted on master and REL_17_STABLE.

As having this coverage may be valuable, there is a discussion on the
thread of possible ways to stabilize the test. If that happens, a fixed
test can be committed again.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P16 tested heap tuple removal with a standby and failed on standby catch-up and row counts. This proposal tests GiST page deletion and reuse, but it also needs vacuum behaviour to be reproducible.

objections.title: Recovery TAP test may duplicate replay that 027_stream_regress.pl already does
objections.failure_scenario: After 0001 lands, src/test/recovery/t/027_stream_regress.pl runs gist.sql on a primary with a streaming standby, so the standby replays the new page deletion and reuse records. 061_gist_crash_recovery.pl then replays the same workload a second time. Every check-world run pays for both, and a later change to the GiST workload must be made in two places.
objections.argument: Postgres already has 027_stream_regress.pl, which runs the main regression suite against a primary with a standby and can enable wal_consistency_checking through PG_TEST_EXTRA. The baseline in llvm-cov-raw.txt (message #1) shows gistxlog.c at about 18%, which suggests the numbers may come from a run without that test. If so, 0001 alone may already cover most of the redo lines credited to 0002. The thread does not compare the two tests or say what 0002 checks that 027 does not, such as crash restart instead of streaming replay.
objections.author_must_show: With 0001 applied and 027_stream_regress.pl included in the coverage run, which gistxlog.c lines does 061_gist_crash_recovery.pl still add?

critic.reasoning: 027_stream_regress.pl replays the main regression suite, including gist.sql, on a standby and can enable wal_consistency_checking through PG_TEST_EXTRA. The 18% baseline for gistxlog.c suggests the coverage run left that test out, and the thread does not say what 0002 adds beyond it.

objections.title: Added runtime of the recovery test and gist.sql steps is not given
objections.failure_scenario: Every developer and CI run of check-world pays for a new crash-restart TAP test with wal_consistency_checking, plus longer gist.sql in each make check. If many coverage patches add tests of this shape each release, suite time grows and slow buildfarm animals time out, as in [P16].
objections.argument: wal_consistency_checking logs full-page images and compares them on replay, which costs more than most recovery tests. No message gives timings for either patch, and no reviewer has asked. The coverage gain is real, mostly in gistxlog.c, but a committer would likely want the cost next to it.
objections.author_must_show: How many seconds do 0001 and 0002 add on a typical machine and on a slow one, and is wal_consistency_checking limited to the GiST workload?

precedents.title: Revert "Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin"

critic.reasoning: No message gives a runtime, and a crash-restart test with wal_consistency_checking is costlier than a plain SQL test, so a committer would likely ask. [P16] timed out on standby catch-up with a large row count and must not be used as support.

objections.title: Page recycling in gist.sql may depend on the xmin horizon of concurrent tests
objections.failure_scenario: gist.sql runs in a parallel group, so another session's open snapshot can hold back the horizon. The second vacuum then leaves deleted pages unrecyclable on some buildfarm animals. Either gist.out differs and the animal goes red, or the test still passes while recycling silently goes unexercised.
objections.argument: A GiST page deleted by vacuum can be recycled only after its deletion XID is older than every snapshot. That depends on what else runs at the time. [P16] was reverted because a vacuum-driven test was "failing to reliably trigger multiple index vacuum rounds" across platforms. The thread does not say how 0001 makes recycling deterministic, and the only report so far is one pass on master in message #4.
objections.author_must_show: How does 0001 make sure deleted pages are recyclable when other tests in the parallel group hold snapshots, and does anything detect when recycling did not happen?

precedents.title: Revert "Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin"

critic.reasoning: GiST recycles a deleted page only once its deletion XID precedes every snapshot, and gist.sql runs in a parallel group. The thread does not say how 0001 makes this deterministic. [P16] failed by a different mechanism, so it is only loose support.

refuted.title: Page recycling in the parallel regression schedule may not happen reliably
refuted.failure_scenario: gist.sql runs in a parallel group, so a concurrent backend's snapshot holds back the xmin horizon and vacuum does not recycle the deleted GiST pages. The expected output can then differ on a slow or 32-bit buildfarm animal. Alternatively it stays the same while the recycle path goes quietly unexercised, and nobody notices the coverage was lost.
refuted.argument: GiST reuses a deleted page only after its deletion XID is older than the global horizon. The thread does not say how 0001 makes that true in a shared regression run. [P16] was a vacuum test reverted for exactly this kind of buildfarm instability. Since index scan and seq scan agree whether or not recycling happens, the comparison cannot detect lost coverage, the weakness [P9] names.
refuted.author_must_show: How does 0001 ensure the deleted pages pass the recycle horizon with concurrent sessions running, and what fails if recycling does not happen?

precedents.title: Revert "Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin"

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1, which quotes [P16] more accurately. [P16] was reverted for standby timeouts and TIDStore row counts, so it is not "exactly this kind" of instability.

precedents_retrieved.title: Sort leaf pages by ctid for gist indexes built using sorting method
precedents_retrieved.summary: For GiST indexes built with the sorted (sortsupport) build method, the patch sorts index tuples on leaf pages by heap TID, so that leaf order follows heap order as it does for indexes built by repeated inserts. The goal was to avoid reading the same heap page more than once and to improve prefetching during scans.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The only reply, from Andrey Borodin, supported the idea, measured roughly a 5% slowdown in CREATE INDEX, and asked for benchmarks showing the scan benefit. The entry was withdrawn the next day with no further message shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

roaster_notes.note: The coverage-only concern from P9 does not apply, because the tests check results and redo. The remaining point is stability, raised above.

The patches change only gist.sql, its expected output and a new recovery TAP test. They add no syntax, GUC, catalog object, dump content, psql behaviour or client-visible change, so nothing in the user-facing contract can break. Test stability and runtime are outside this angle.

The patches only add tests and change no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, protocol or extension API. Whether page recycling is deterministic under the parallel regression schedule is a test-stability question (see [P16]), and other angles cover it.

The patches are test-only: they add steps to gist.sql and a new recovery TAP test, with no change to server code, privileges, roles, defaults, authentication or exposed information. There is no privilege or exposure aspect to review from the security angle.
The proposal is test-only and fits core. Both objections concern test stability and cost and can be fixed in a new version.
0001 extends the existing gist.sql test and has no alternative elsewhere. Only 0002 overlaps with an existing mechanism.

No demand objection: the patch is test-only, and its beneficiaries are Postgres developers, who need tests for GiST redo, which ran at about 18% coverage. Runtime cost and test stability belong to other angles, and the thread does not report the added runtime.
